messages.author: 120aaddd58a60b60
messages.subject: Best practice to (re)use RJDBC / SQL server connections in Shiny app
parts:
Hello,

I've also posted a similar question at SO (http://stackoverflow.com/questions/18552878/are-there-performance-other-downsides-in-creating-a-new-rjdbc-connections-to-ms) but so far hasn't got any response there.

I'm trying to understand what's the best practice to (re)using RJDBC connection to SQL Server. Is my understanding correct that shiny will create a new process for every new client connection, and therefore it's a bad practice to initialize an RJDBC connection in global.R and the reuse it among all clients?

I know that R is single-threaded, so I don't really understand how is it possible for Shiny to initialize all the variables in global.R only once and still have a process for  every client?

Any advice or explanation how Shiny works w.r.t. multi-threading will be greatly appreciated!

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Best practice to (re)use RJDBC / SQL server connections in Shiny app
parts:
My experience with RDBMS is all from the Java world, not R, but in general I don't think it's a good idea to use a connection across multiple users, whether single-threaded or not. Transaction scope is tied to a connection so you really only want to use a connection for the lifetime of something you could consider a logical transaction.

Performance-wise you would want your DB driver or framework to implement connection pooling for you, so opening "new connection" from your code would not be too expensive. However I don't know if RJDBC implements connection pooling or not--I see no evidence of this. Still, I'd start with relatively short-lived, isolated connections until you see that there is a performance/scalability problem.
